properties.note: World's largest offshore oil field (Arabian Gulf); heavy Arab grades for Gulf and Asian refiners.

properties.name: Rumaila
properties.operator: Rumaila Operating Organization (owner: Basra Oil Company)
properties.note: Backbone of Basrah crude exports, which depend on Hormuz transit.

properties.name: West Qurna

output.n: West Qurna-2 only, a share only of the field; estimate of 460,000 to 480,000 b/d (midpoint) in The National, 10 February 2026 (https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/energy/2026/02/10/iraq-tightens-control-over-west-qurna-2-oilfield-as-sanctions-force-lukoil-retreat)

properties.note: Super-giant in southern Iraq feeding Basrah exports (Hormuz transit). The output figure is for West Qurna-2: Lukoil, the majority stakeholder, has left amid US sanctions and Basrah Oil Company runs the field through interim operators (The National). Operator, owner and location: Wikipedia, West Qurna field.

capacity.n: infobox oil production, year not stated; as stated by the source

properties.note: Offshore Abu Dhabi giant owned by ADNOC (ExxonMobil 28%, JODCO 12%).

properties.name: Tengiz

capacity.n: infobox oil production (the infobox gives 2025 as the peak year), year of the figure not stated; as stated by the source

properties.note: Source of CPC Blend; exports via the CPC pipeline to Novorossiysk.

properties.name: Kashagan
properties.note: Offshore North Caspian.

properties.name: Johan Sverdrup
properties.statusNote: Listed as producing by the Norwegian Offshore Directorate
properties.note: Largest North Sea field; Johan Sverdrup grade is a Dated Brent basket component. Position is the centre of the field outline of the Norwegian Offshore Directorate (the Wikipedia infobox point is about 45 km to the north). Status: Norwegian Offshore Directorate FactMaps, read in November 2026.

properties.name: Stabroek Block (Liza, Payara, Yellowtail)

capacity.n: Guyana's installed production capacity after the fifth Stabroek project (Uaru), ExxonMobil, 16 November 2026 (https://corporate.exxonmobil.com/news/news-releases/2026/1116-exxonmobil-starts-production-at-uaru); the release names the Destiny, Unity, Prosperity, ONE GUYANA and Errea Wittu vessels

properties.note: Fastest-growing new supply source. Wikipedia (Petroleum industry in Guyana) gives Guyana's output of about 660 kb/d by 2024 (national figure); the capacity figure is the national installed capacity stated by ExxonMobil. Operator shares, opening year and location: Wikipedia, Petroleum industry in Guyana.

properties.name: Buzios
properties.statusNote: Production figure of 2024 in the Wikipedia infobox
properties.note: Pre-salt Santos Basin; key driver of Brazilian crude exports.

properties.name: Tupi (Lula)
properties.statusNote: Production figure of 2025 in the Wikipedia infobox
properties.note: Largest Brazilian pre-salt field.

properties.name: Samotlor
properties.note: Legacy West Siberian giant in decline.

properties.name: Vankor
properties.note: Feeds the Transneft/ESPO system. No production figure given.

properties.name: Daqing
properties.note: China's largest oil field.

properties.name: North Field / South Pars

output.n: Qatari side (North Field), early 2026 before the war, "about 18.5 billion cubic feet per day" (the Iranian side is in South Pars (Iranian side))

properties.note: World's largest gas field, shared by Qatar and Iran; feeds Ras Laffan LNG. The figure is the Qatari side. The article gives Iranian output of about 2 Bcf/d in early 2026, before the war (see South Pars, Iranian side). For the Qatari side the article says only that 10,000 employees were evacuated and activities shut down during the war, without a date or an end, so no status is given; the strike of 18 March 2026 hit the Iranian side.

capacity.n: nominal production capacity, as stated by the source

properties.note: Yamal Peninsula; supplies the Yamal-Europe line and the domestic grid. The article says deeper layers could raise capacity to 140 bcm/y.

properties.name: Troll
properties.statusNote: Listed as producing by the Norwegian Offshore Directorate
properties.note: Anchor of Norwegian gas exports to the EU and the UK via Langeled, Europipe and Norpipe. No production figure given.

properties.name: Zohr

output.n: August 2019 output; declined later per source

properties.note: Egypt's largest gas field. About 190 km north of Port Said per the source.

properties.name: Hassi Messaoud

capacity.n: current production in the infobox, as stated by the source; no year given

properties.note: Algeria's largest oil field, operated and owned by Sonatrach. Position is the town of Hassi Messaoud; production began in 1960 (Wikipedia, Hassi Messaoud oil field).

properties.name: Hassi R'Mel

capacity.n: annual producing capacity, as stated by the source; no year given

properties.note: Algeria's main gas field and hub for the Transmed, Medgaz and GME pipelines to Europe. The article gives an annual producing capacity of about 100 billion cubic metres.

properties.name: Permian Basin
properties.operator: Many operators (a basin, not a single asset)

output.n: oil, June 2024 (estimate in the report released 13 May 2024), EIA Drilling Productivity Report, Permian region (https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/drilling/)

properties.note: Largest US tight-oil basin; the driver of US crude and associated-gas growth. A basin, not a single asset. Location: Wikipedia, Permian Basin (North America).

properties.name: Marcellus Shale (Appalachian Basin)
properties.operator: Many operators (a basin, not a single asset)

output.n: gas, June 2024 (estimate in the report released 13 May 2024), EIA Drilling Productivity Report, Appalachia region (Marcellus and Utica) (https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/drilling/)

properties.note: Largest US shale-gas play by output. The EIA figure covers the whole Appalachia region, which includes the Utica. Location: Wikipedia, Marcellus Formation.

properties.name: Haynesville Shale
properties.operator: Many operators (a basin, not a single asset)

output.n: gas, June 2024 (estimate in the report released 13 May 2024), EIA Drilling Productivity Report, Haynesville region (https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/drilling/)

properties.note: Swing gas play feeding Gulf Coast LNG export plants. Location: Wikipedia, Haynesville Shale.

properties.name: Vaca Muerta

output.n: natural gas, September 2024: Vaca Muerta was 74% of Argentina's gas output, 3.8 Bcf/d (EIA, Today in Energy, 5 December 2024: https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=63924)

properties.note: Argentina's shale play; fastest-growing Latin American supply after pre-salt and Guyana. The EIA gives Vaca Muerta 58% of the country's oil (738 kb/d in September 2024) without a field figure in barrels. Operator, opening year and location: Wikipedia, Vaca Muerta.

properties.name: Orinoco Belt (Faja Petrolifera)
properties.note: Extra-heavy crude belt; the source gives a resource estimate of 1.3 trillion barrels in place, no production figure.

properties.name: Ahvaz
properties.operator: National Iranian South Oil Company (NISOC), for NIOC

output.n: oil, "as of September 2016"; the infobox gives 750 kb/d without a year

properties.note: Iran's largest single oil field according to the article, which says production is in decline.

properties.name: Athabasca oil sands
properties.operator: Syncrude, Suncor Energy, Canadian Natural Resources, TotalEnergies, Imperial Oil, Petro-Canada, Devon, Husky, Statoil, Nexen (infobox)

output.n: all Canadian oil sands, not the Athabasca deposit alone (basis not stated): the article says oil sands production reached 3.1 million barrels per day in 2018; its infobox gives 2.8 million for the deposit

properties.note: Alberta bitumen mines and in situ projects, a region rather than a single asset. Production began in 1967 with the Great Canadian Oil Sands plant. Position is the point of the infobox, not a site.

properties.note: Offshore field in the Bay of Campeche, about 105 km from Ciudad del Carmen. Mexico's largest field. Position is Ciudad del Carmen, the nearest town, not the field. Coordinates: OpenStreetMap.

properties.note: The article carries a "needs more citations" tag and an unsourced paragraph that gives 400 to 450 kb/d.

capacity.n: current output in the infobox, as stated by the source; no year given

properties.name: Bakken (Williston Basin)
properties.operator: Many operators (a basin, not a single asset)

properties.name: South Pars (Iranian side)
properties.operator: National Iranian Oil Company; Pars Oil and Gas Company runs the South Pars projects

output.n: gas, early 2026 before the war, "about 2 billion cubic feet per day"

properties.statusNote: Several gas phases shut after the attack of 18 March 2026 (Wikipedia)
properties.note: Iranian part of the field shared with Qatar. Gas production started with phase 2 in December 2002. The article says an attack on 18 March 2026 shut several gas phases (about 12% of Iran's gas output in the first reports). Position is the Asaluyeh district, the onshore hub, not the offshore field.
